ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as an NS-7 voucher; send the driver's account to Ryde review for the fake "I'm Here" confirmation tapped 351 m from the pickup point + flag_account
ruling.reasoning: The dispute is a driver-cancelled no-show: the driver cancelled at 08:51:00 and a $6.61 cancellation fee stands on the record [F3][F6], so it can only survive if all of NS-1's conditions are met [NS-0]. NS-0 routes this branch to NS-1/NS-2, and the trace and facts settle every element: arrival was confirmed by a driver tap at 08:47:20 [F5] (NS-1 (i) satisfied), but at that moment the driver was 351 m from the pickup point and his closest approach across the whole trip was 319 m at 08:46:50 [F5][F1], so NS-1 (ii) fails; and after the tap he spent 0 s continuously inside the radius, his 4 min 0 s stationary period (08:47:00–08:51:00) being spent about 350 m away [F5][F2], so NS-1 (iii) also fails [NS-1]. With (ii) and (iii) unmet, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full [NS-2]. The driver's "Reached already" chat message at 08:47 [F8] and his post-trip statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes at the pickup [F12] cannot establish the no-show, because system GPS and timeline records outrank statements and place him outside the pickup radius throughout [F1][F4][F5]. No traffic incident, speed band or weather condition provides any excuse [F13][F14][F15], though none was claimed [NS-1]. The rider's own messages show she was at the pickup point and asked where the car was at 08:48 [F9], after which the driver cancelled at 08:51 [F10][F3] — nothing she did forfeits the fee, so the refund is owed. Amount: the trace fixes it at the recorded cancellation fee, $6.61, with surge 1.0× and no added charge [F6][F7][NS-2][NS-7]; delivered as a Ryde voucher [NS-7]. Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, NS-2 additionally directs an account flag [F5][F1][NS-2]. Profiles (rider 1 dispute, 0 upheld [F16]; driver long clean history [F17]) are not used to decide the fee. Safety screen: I read every chat message [F8][F9][F10], the driver's statement [F12] and the complaint — nothing is threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexual or a dangerous-driving allegation; the messages are a pickup-location disagreement only [SAFE-1]. Evidence is complete: continuous GPS/timeline coverage of the wait with no hole [F5], every chat message timestamped [F11], cancellation side and fee recorded [F3][F6].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's profile (1,346 days, 4.85 rating, 992 trips, 0 upheld disputes [F17]) cannot create or preserve a fee the conditions of NS-1 never authorised; profile facts may not decide the case, and the GPS/timeline records place him outside the pickup radius throughout [F1][F2][F5][NS-1][NS-2]. His own brief resolves to refund_full, so no leniency outcome preserving the fee is available.

The driver's argument that no longer no-show threshold was met is correct on the facts — 7 min from acceptance to cancellation [F3] and 4 min 0 s stationary [F2] — but it defeats his position, not the rider's: NS-1 (iii) is measured as continuous waiting inside the radius after the arrival confirmation, and that is 0 s [F5][NS-1]. No threshold in the record needed to be reached for NS-2 to require the refund [NS-2].

The absence of traffic incidents, speed bands and bad weather [F13][F14][F15] is neutral — no reasonable-cause excuse was claimed — and it does not affect the outcome, which is governed by the failed NS-1 (ii)/(iii) elements [F5][F1][F2][NS-1][NS-2].

This claim concedes NS-1 (ii) fails (closest approach 319 m [F1], no driver_arrived_at recorded [F4]) and therefore supports the rider's refund rather than the driver's; it is rejected only as a ground for any outcome other than refund_full under NS-2.
